resources.string: In Desktop Mode, BentoBar dynamically adjusts to fit within the top bar of floating windows alongside the icon and name of the app, and the minimize, close, and, maximize buttons whenever it would obstruct them. This is to be used when the system hides or disables the status bar at the top of the screen in its desktop windowing mode.
Keep clear at a window\'s left
Keep clear at a window\'s right
Where this item goes while Desktop Mode is active, so it can show or hide along with the status bar.
When BentoBar\'s icons would collide with a window\'s title bar, they keep showing and lie over the app\'s icon and name instead of being hidden. They never cover the window\'s buttons.
Distance from the top in Desktop Mode
What you put in each card here is where the item goes while Desktop Mode is active. The order is shared with the regular bar.
While a window is maximized (it fills the screen above the taskbar), BentoBar steps aside, since an app\'s own top bar would lie under it. It comes back when the window is smaller.
Items with a Show when… rule sit where they will pop in.
